mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher than baseline during low rates (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not follow low unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong demand in the housing market, leading to positive economic growth and S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts rise but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in industrial production (INDPRO) signals increased economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth does not correlate with positive returns (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in federal funds rate above 0.25% signals monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns remain positive when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.25% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment (PAYEMS) and low unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not follow strong labor market signals (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1) and low unemployment (UNRATE) indicate high demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth and low unemployment do not lead to positive returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, low unemployment (UNRATE) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL) may lead to monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns do not follow late-cycle signals (Rank IC < 0.03).
